axle.carrier.carrier.name: Differential carrier
axle.carrier.carrier.notes: The nose piece: round flange on the ten case studs with a spigot into the banjo opening, the tapering nose with four ribs carrying the two pinion bearing cups and the oil seal, and behind the flange the two saddles (with lightening windows) for the differential bearings under their caps. Withdrawn forward after the axleshafts, the propeller shaft and the nuts and spring washers (Sec 8 paras 1-3). Everything behind the flange passes through the case's 205 mm opening. Nose length from Fig 8.1 (about the flange's width) set so the pinion flange lands where the propeller shaft is at its supplier length; the cast surfaces from Fig 8.1 item 13 (no outside photographs could be opened from the build machine).

specs.ref: Case ring round the 205 mm opening

specs.label: Pinion flange face
specs.ref: Forward of the axle centre: propeller shaft at 31 1/8 in (propshaft_layout)

Spiral (hypoid) teeth on the head, the rear bearing seat behind the head, the shank, the front bearing seat, the splines for the flange and the 3/4 in UNF thread for the nut. Hypoid offset, pitch sizes and spiral angle derived.

axle.casing.case.name: Axle case (banjo)
axle.casing.case.material: Pressed and welded steel, forged ends
axle.casing.case.notes: Banjo case of two pressings welded on the horizontal centre line (the seam bead, drawn as the serrated line in Fig 8.1), a ring round the front opening with the ten gear carrier studs, the necks and tubes, forged ends welded in: brake backplate flange (four lobes), the hub oil seal track (1 15/16 in, the seal's bore), the 40 mm hub bearing journal and the bearing nut thread - left-hand on the left, right-hand on the right (mgaguru.com hub_06; BritishCarForum) - with a keyway for the locking washer's tab. Spring seats welded under the tubes (the locating plate, pad, spring and damper bracket go under them, Ch 11 Fig 11.4); a bracket under each tube with the rebound strap spindle (Fig 8.1 item 5 is its nut; Ch 8 Sec 3 para 4 'check straps ... on the anchor pins'); bosses for the breather on top (Sec 2 para 3), the combined filler/level plug on the rear face (Sec 2 para 1) and the drain plug; a tab for the brake pipe three-way union and the pin for the handbrake balance lever (Sec 3 paras 4-5; their parts are P8). Lubricant 2.25 Imp pints (p142). Positions of the seats, brackets, tab and pin are derived; the hand of each thread follows the references above (see PLAN questions).

specs.label: Tube diameter
specs.ref: Fig 8.1 proportions against the 80 mm hub bearing

specs.label: Width over backplate faces
specs.ref: Drum inside the inner half of the 4 1/2J rim on the 49.25 in track (rear_axle_layout)

specs.label: Thread diameter
specs.ref: Inside the 40 mm bearing bore, 16 tpi

axle.casing.filler-plug.name: Filler and level plug
axle.casing.filler-plug.notes: Combined filler/level plug on the rear face; top up to the level of the plug and let any excess run out before refitting (Sec 2 para 1).

axle.carrier.crown-wheel-lockwasher.notes: Tab plate under each pair of bolt heads, the tabs turned up against the flats (Fig 8.1 item 29).

axle.hubs.axleshaft.name: Axleshaft (wire wheels)
axle.hubs.axleshaft.notes: Splined at both ends: the inner end into the differential wheel, the outer into the hub extension; no flange on the wire wheel shaft. Withdrawn after the drum and the hub extension, noting the O-ring seal (Sec 4 paras 5-6). Jack up that side first so the oil does not reach the linings (para 1).

axle.hubs.hub.notes: A bell over the bearing on the end of the case, the oil seal in its inner end, a lobed flange with the four studs for the drum and hub extension and the tapped hole for the extension screw. Drawn off with a puller complete with the bearing and seal (Sec 5 para 3). The bearing's outer face stands 0.001 to 0.004 in proud of the hub so the extension's flange clamps it against the shoulder (para 4d).

specs.label: Bearing bore
specs.note: Rear hub bearing 2K7477 (LDJ40 / 4208), 3.1496 in (80.0 mm) OD

specs.label: Bearing proud
specs.note: Sec 5 para 4d: outer bearing face protrudes 0.001 to 0.004 in (0.025 to 0.102 mm)

axle.hubs.hub-extension-rh.name: Hub extension, RH (wire wheels)

partNumbers.by: BMC (MGOC Spares: wire wheel hub, 12 TPI, RH, Mk1)

axle.hubs.hub-extension-rh.notes: On the right-hand hub. Flange on the hub studs (the brake drum over it, four nuts) and held by the countersunk screw; the inner cone the wheel centre seats on, 42 mm series Rudge-Whitworth splines and the spinner thread - left-hand on the car's right-hand side (MGOC "wheel spinners"), 12 tpi on cars to GHN3-30850 (about February 1964; MGOC, S C Parts 6954). body.doors.quarter-light-frame-l.name: Quarter-light frame, left

body.doors.glass-channel-r.name: Door glass rear run channel, right

body.doors.quarter-light-seal-l.name: Quarter-light front seal, left

specs.ref: Oliver's photo 09: a dark line between the pillar and the frame

body.doors.pull-handle-l.name: Exterior pull handle, left

body.doors.mirror.notes: Rectangular chrome mirror head with rounded corners on a flat arm from a clamp on the right-hand quarter-light's rear post (Oliver's photos 08, 15, 23).

specs.ref: Oliver's photo 08 against the quarter-light post

body.front.front-wing-l.name: Front wing, left

specs.label: Half width
specs.note: Overall width 59.9 in over the body sides

specs.ref: profile photo 29 scaled on the wheelbase: a circle fitted to the arch edge, centre 8 mm behind the hub

body.front.grille-panel.name: Grille panel (front panel)
body.front.grille-panel.notes: The front panel between the wing fronts and below the bonnet's front edge, round the grille opening (a wide shallow rounded rectangle, its top following the bonnet's front edge just below the headlamp centres, its foot behind the bumper blade; Oliver's photos 10, 15, 27, 28).

body.front.front-valance.name: Front valance
body.front.front-valance.notes: The apron under the bumper across the front, from the valance seam down to the lower edge, the arches' fronts.

specs.label: Seam height
specs.ref: Above the road, behind the bumper blade (profile photo 29: blade 356-404)

body.front.bonnet-skin.name: Bonnet (outer skin)

specs.label: Rear edge x
specs.ref: Ahead of the scuttle, 8 mm ahead of the bulkhead's top

body.front.scuttle.name: Scuttle top
body.front.scuttle.notes: Scuttle top panel from the bonnet's rear gap to the cockpit's front edge over the facia, between the wing seams, rising to P10's screen base; the two wiper spindle holes (P10 WIPER_SPINDLES).

body.front.bonnet-frame.name: Bonnet inner frame
body.front.bonnet-frame.notes: Stiffening frame under the skin: a 54 mm perimeter band following the skin 22 mm under it, a cross brace over the rocker cover and a centre rib forward to the lock pin.

specs.label: Band width
specs.ref: Inside the 4 mm gap, 6 to 60 mm in from the edge

body.front.bonnet-hinge-l.name: Bonnet hinge, left
body.front.bonnet-hinge-l.notes: Bracket on the scuttle under the bonnet's rear edge, the arm to the frame with two bolts, nuts and washers (Sec 6 para 1).

body.front.bonnet-stay.name: Bonnet stay
body.front.bonnet-stay.notes: Prop rod stowed along the left inner wing in its clip (Sec 6 para 1).

body.rear.boot-lock.notes: Lock inside the lid's rear panel; the striker on the rear panel's top edge.

body.rear.boot-carpet.name: Boot floor carpet
body.rear.boot-carpet.notes: Black carpet on the boot floor under the spare wire wheel (Oliver's photo 26), cut round the wheel's locating ring.

body.structure.toe-board-l.name: Toe board, left

specs.ref: underbody_layout TOE_FOOT (P11a, from P8's brake pipe run)

body.structure.toe-board-r.name: Toe board, right

The pedal box aperture inside the box's rear flange with its six bolt holes (P8 parts/brakes/master.py box_bolts; nuts behind the panel), the heater air opening on the centre line (early heater, Fig 12.27), the main harness grommet (P10 HARNESS_GROMMET) and three smaller grommet holes for the speedometer cable, oil gauge pipe and temperature capillary on the right, the four-way connection's bolt hole (P8 FOUR_WAY), the overdrive vacuum switch's screw holes (P10), the steering column hole (P9) and the fuel pipe clip screws (P11a CLIPS).

body.structure.column-toe-mount.name: Steering column lower mounting cup
body.structure.column-toe-mount.notes: Pressed cup welded to the bulkhead's cabin face, its face square to the column at P9's COLUMN_TOE_PLATE (40 mm behind the bulkhead), with the hole for the 1 1/2 in tube and the bottom bracket's two stud holes. P9 placed the bracket on "the toe board"; the toe board (P11a datums) is lower here, so the body carries this cup.

body.structure.clutch-hose-support.name: Clutch hose bracket support
body.structure.clutch-hose-support.notes: Angle welded to the bulkhead's engine face under P4's pipe-to-hose bracket (clutch_layout HOSE_BRACKET), one 1/4 in screw. P9 suggested moving the bracket to the chassis leg; the leg is 160 mm outboard of it, so the bracket keeps its place and the body supports it (see PLAN).

specs.label: Arm length
specs.ref: Bulkhead face to the bracket plus its foot

body.structure.scuttle-inner.name: Scuttle inner panel and facia rail
body.structure.scuttle-inner.notes: Closing panel under the scuttle top from the bulkhead flange back to ahead of P10's instrument cases, 58 mm under the top, with the wiper wheelbox holes (P10 WIPER_SPINDLES), and the square-section rail under the scuttle's rear edge, above the instruments, tying the kick panels together (MGBs Made in Australia).

specs.label: Depth below scuttle
specs.ref: Room for the wheelboxes and rack tubes (P10)

body.structure.wiper-motor-bracket.name: Wiper motor bracket
body.structure.wiper-motor-bracket.notes: Hung from the scuttle inner panel on the left for P10's DR3A motor (WIPER_MOTOR), three screw holes.

body.structure.column-top-bracket.name: Steering column upper bracket
body.structure.column-top-bracket.notes: Pressed channel hung from the facia rail; the column clamp (Fig 11.6 item 59) bolts under it at P9's COLUMN_TOP_CLAMP.

specs.label: Bolt spacing
specs.ref: Clamp's two bolts either side of the column

body.structure.front-leg-l.name: Front chassis leg, left
body.structure.front-leg-l.notes: Box-section member along the engine bay floor: level over the front crossmember with its underside on P9's upper rubber pads (front_suspension_layout BODY_FACE_Z) and top at BODY_LEG_TOP_Z where the support bolt nuts sit, holes and a spacer tube at both support bolts (BODY_BOLTS), forward to the front apron with the bumper spring bar bolt holes, back under the toe board and the floor to a third of the way along the door ("case of the bends": the front chassis member ends at the jacking aperture level). Ahead of and behind the crossmember the leg steps inboard to |y| 338 and narrows to 62 mm: the tyre's shoulder at full lock (28 deg front in, 37 deg rear in, for the published 32 ft turning circle) sweeps through the straight line, and P8's right front pipe runs at y -300 beside it.

body.structure.inner-wing-l.name: Inner wing and wheel house, left
body.structure.inner-wing-l.notes: Engine-bay valance at body_layout INNER_WING_Y from the bulkhead to the front apron, from the leg to the wing bolting flange; the wheel house arched over the tyre (420 mm about the axle) out to the outer wing; the damper arm opening (P9: the arm sweeps over the leg between |y| 305 and 499); the brake hose bracket hole (P9 HOSE_BRACKET); the overdrive relay's screws (P10 OD_RELAY).

specs.label: Wheel house radius
specs.ref: Tyre radius 309 plus bump travel and clearance

body.structure.inner-wing-r.name: Inner wing and wheel house, right
body.structure.inner-wing-r.notes: Mirror of the left with the screws for P10's control box, fuse block, flasher and starter solenoid.

body.structure.front-apron.name: Front apron and radiator duct
body.structure.front-apron.notes: The vertical cross panel behind the bumper the horns bolt to (P10 HORN_PANEL_X, HORN_POS), between the legs; the radiator duct's floor running back from the grille opening to the radiator's front face with the grille's three bottom bolt holes (Sec 7 para 1), and the duct's side panels.

body.structure.lock-platform.name: Bonnet lock platform
body.structure.lock-platform.notes: Cross panel over the grille opening under the bonnet's front edge: the lock's three bolt holes and locating cup hole (Sec 6 para 4, photo 6.4), the grille steady brackets' three screw holes (Sec 7 para 1).

body.structure.inner-sill-l.name: Inner sill, left
body.structure.inner-sill-l.notes: Inner skin of the boxed sill at underbody_layout SILL_Y from below the floor to the tread, the tread turned out to the door shut line, the closing flange underneath, the jacking socket hole.

specs.label: Tread height
specs.ref: Above the road: the door bottom shuts outboard of it

body.structure.castle-l.name: Sill castle section, left
body.structure.castle-l.notes: The sill's middle member (three-member boxed sills, 'case of the bends'): a vertical web with flanged castellations top and bottom.

specs.label: Tabs
specs.ref: Castellations each side along the sill

specs.label: Tabs
specs.ref: Castellations each side along the sill

body.structure.jack-socket-l.name: Jacking socket, left
body.structure.jack-socket-l.notes: Square tube through the sill box a third of the way along the door ('jacking apertures', case of the bends).

body.structure.hinge-pillar-l.name: Hinge pillar, left
body.structure.hinge-pillar-l.notes: Shut face at the door's front shut line with the two hinges' three bolt holes each (Sec 32), the kick panel inboard.

specs.label: Hinge heights
specs.ref: Above the road, lower and upper hinges

body.structure.shut-pillar-l.name: Shut pillar, left
body.structure.shut-pillar-l.notes: Panel at the door's rear shut line with the striker plate's three screw holes (Sec 27).

specs.label: Striker height
specs.ref: Above the road, at the lock

body.structure.heelboard.name: Heelboard
body.structure.heelboard.notes: Riser behind the seats, rear face at underbody_layout HEELBOARD_X, floor to tonneau floor, sill to sill, the propeller shaft's tunnel opening, a swage, the fuel pump bracket's two captive-nut holes (P11a pump.py BRACKET_BOLT_Y/Z; Haynes Ch 3 Sec 5: the pump on the heelboard by the RH spring) and the fuel hose union's hole (MAIN_START).

body.structure.tonneau-floor.name: Tonneau (rear) floor
body.structure.tonneau-floor.notes: Floor behind the seats over P10's two battery carriers (body_layout TONNEAU_FLOOR_Z): an aperture over each carrier, the carriers' four flange bolt holes each, the damper access grommet holes (Ch 11 photo 2.4 "access grommet for rear hydraulic shock absorbers, adjacent to the battery access apertures"), two pressed ribs.

body.structure.battery-cover-l.name: Battery access cover, left
body.structure.battery-cover-l.notes: Cover over the left aperture with two quick-release screws (Ch 10 Sec 2 para 1).

body.structure.battery-cover-r.name: Battery access cover, right
body.structure.battery-cover-r.notes: Mirror of the left (the 12 V battery's side).

body.structure.rear-bulkhead.name: Rear bulkhead
body.structure.rear-bulkhead.notes: The boot's front wall behind the hood stowage well, from the tonneau floor up under the rear deck, a swage.

specs.label: X
specs.ref: Behind the dampers and battery carriers, ahead of the axle arch

body.structure.rear-wheelhouse-l.name: Rear wheel house, left
body.structure.rear-wheelhouse-l.notes: Inner wall at |y| 498 outboard of the rear rail, the arched band over the tyre (430 mm about the axle: the tyre at full bump) out to the outer wing.

specs.label: Radius
specs.ref: Tyre radius plus P9's bump travel (52 mm gap, 44 mm rubber) and clearance

body.structure.boot-floor.name: Boot floor
body.structure.boot-floor.notes: Kick-up over the axle (underside at underbody_layout ARCH_Z, P9's bump strike) with a hump over the differential that carries P8's rear hose bracket, stepping down behind the axle to the floor over the tank (BOOT_FLOOR_Z) to the rear panel; the filler stub's hole (P11a FILLER; Fig 3.9 item 12 seal), the spare wheel's pressed locating ring and clamp stud hole, the exhaust rear bracket's two captive-nut holes (P11a), two drain holes.

body.structure.tank-tabs.name: Fuel tank strap tabs
body.structure.tank-tabs.notes: Pairs of tabs for P11a's strap front clevis pins on the boot floor step (STRAP_PIN_FRONT) and rear hanger pins under the floor (HANGER_PIN), at both straps.

specs.label: Pin hole
specs.ref: Clearance for the 1/4 in clevis pins (MGOC CLZ427)

body.structure.rear-rail-l.name: Rear chassis rail, left
body.structure.rear-rail-l.notes: Box section from the heelboard to the rear panel, kicked up over the axle (its underside the bump rubber strike face, P9 BUMP_STRIKE, with a strike plate), with the damper doubler and its two bolt holes on the inner face (P9 DAMPER_MOUNT, DAMPER_FACE_Y 436), the spring's front hanger plates (FRONT_HANGER), the rear shackle bracket (SHACKLE_BRACKET) and the rebound strap bracket (REBOUND_BOLT).

body.structure.rear-hose-bracket.name: Rear brake hose bracket
body.structure.rear-hose-bracket.notes: Angle under the boot floor's differential hump at P8's REAR_HOSE_BRACKET; the hose's locknut hole.

specs.label: Hole
specs.ref: Hose end's 3/8 in UNF thread and locknut

body.structure.handbrake-abutment.name: Handbrake cable abutment bracket
body.structure.handbrake-abutment.notes: Bracket inside the tunnel's right wall behind the operating lever, the outer cable's ferrule hole (P8 CABLE_ABUTMENT, 'A' in Fig 9.10).

body.structure.cable-grommet.name: Battery cable grommet
body.structure.cable-grommet.notes: Rubber grommet in the right toe board for P10's battery cable (CABLE_GROMMET).

body.structure.harness-grommets.name: Harness grommets (rear and tunnel)
body.structure.harness-grommets.notes: Rubber grommets where P10b's wiring passes the body (mgb/wiring_layout.py routes): the rear harness through the rear bulkhead beside the right wheel house, the fuel pump lead through the heelboard, the tank unit lead down through the boot floor, the overdrive leads through the tunnel's front, the dip switch leads up through the right toe board. The main harness grommet in the bulkhead is P10b's (electrical.loom.bulkhead-grommet); the body has its hole.

specs.label: Bore
specs.ref: Sized round the largest bundle through each

body.structure.harness-clips.name: Harness P-clips
body.structure.harness-clips.notes: Steel P-clips holding P10b's harness to the body: along the inner wing tops (z 118, |y| 405), across the front panel behind the grille (x 560, z -40), behind the facia (x -655, z 277), down the right sill (y -591, z -350) and in the boot, each on a self-tapping screw (positions on the harness nodes, mgb/wiring_layout.py).

body.structure.outer-sill-l.name: Outer sill, left
body.structure.outer-sill-l.notes: The sill's outer skin between the wheel arches below the door (the outer member of the three-member boxed sill), the body surface below the sill seam (body_shell_layout SILL_TOP_H), tucked under to the closing flange.

specs.label: Seam height
specs.ref: Above the road; the door's bottom edge 7 mm above it

body.structure.arch-liners.name: Wheel arch returns
body.structure.arch-liners.notes: A band just inside each wing's arch opening, from the skin in toward the wheel house, in underseal (the arches read dark inside in Oliver's photos 02, 09, 23).

specs.label: Depth
specs.ref: Skin to the wheel house wall

brakes.front.disc.name: Brake disc
brakes.front.disc.notes: Hat-section disc: the centre plate with four bolt holes stands outboard and seats on the back of the hub flange, the hat wall runs back to the swept ring (Fig 9.7). Bolted to the hub with four bolts, washers and nuts; mark disc and hub before parting them (Sec 11 para 4). Run-out 0.006 in maximum. Hat depth, bore, bolt circle and the heat groove derived.

brakes.front.disc-bolt.name: Disc to hub bolt
brakes.front.disc-bolt.notes: Head inside the disc's hat, through the centre plate and the hub flange; 3/8 UNF from the MGOC nut. Length derived.

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Disc plate, hub flange, washer and nut

brakes.front.dust-cover-lh.name: Disc dust cover (stone guard), LH

partNumbers.by: MGOC Spares (back plate, L/H; black or stainless)

brakes.front.dust-cover-lh.notes: Dished pressing behind the disc with an open sector round the caliper, pressed radial ribs and a rolled rim (Fig 9.7), held to the swivel axle by three screws and spring washers. Screw positions and sizes derived.

brakes.front.dust-cover-rh.name: Disc dust cover (stone guard), RH
brakes.front.dust-cover-rh.notes: Mirror image of the LH cover.

partNumbers.by: MGOC Spares (hex head screw, 5/16 UNF x 1/2)

brakes.front.caliper-mounting-half-lh.name: Caliper mounting half, LH
brakes.front.caliper-mounting-half-lh.notes: Inboard half: cylinder block with the 54 mm bore, the fluid seal groove and the dust seal recess in its mouth (Fig 9.8), a raised boss on its back; cheeks guiding the pads and the bridge bosses over the disc; the two mounting lugs (tapped for the caliper bolts from behind the swivel axle), the hose union on its inboard face, the bleed screw on top, the fluid port across the joint with its seal. The caliper sits behind the axle (Figs 9.2, 9.3). Shape from Figs 9.7 and 9.8; outside sizes derived; the halves are never to be separated in service.

brakes.front.caliper-mounting-half-rh.name: Caliper mounting half, RH
brakes.front.caliper-mounting-half-rh.notes: Mirror image of the LH half (Fig 9.7 draws the RH caliper).

brakes.front.caliper-rim-half-lh.name: Caliper rim half, LH
brakes.front.caliper-rim-half-lh.notes: Outboard half: as the mounting half without the lugs and union, clearance holes and spot faces for the bridge bolt heads, the plug (14) in its top boss.

brakes.front.caliper-rim-half-rh.name: Caliper rim half, RH
brakes.front.caliper-rim-half-rh.notes: Mirror image of the LH rim half.

brakes.front.bridge-bolt.name: Caliper bridge bolt

partNumbers.by: MGOC Spares (bridge bolt; 35.5 to 37 lbf ft)

brakes.front.bridge-bolt.notes: Two per caliper, through the rim half into the mounting half beside the pad aperture. Size (7/16 UNF) and length derived; not shown in Haynes.

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Rim half spot face into the mounting half

partNumbers.by: MGOC Spares (bridge seal for caliper halves, fluid channel)

brakes.front.piston.name: Caliper piston
brakes.front.piston.notes: Hollow, the open end on the pad; the relieved face toward the hub centre (Fig 9.6, Sec 10 para 4), set 1/4 in proud of the cylinder when fitting the dust seal (Sec 12 para 4).

brakes.front.pad.name: Brake pad backing plate
brakes.front.pad.notes: Renew all four pads together (Sec 2 para 1). Outline from Fig 9.7 with the lug the clip bears on; size derived.

specs.label: Thickness
specs.ref: Fig 9.8 scaled to the 54 mm piston

brakes.front.anti-squeal-shim.name: Anti-squeal shim
brakes.front.anti-squeal-shim.notes: Thin plate between piston and pad backing, its arrow upward. Not in the Haynes figure.

brakes.front.pad-clip.name: Pad retaining spring clip

partNumbers.by: MGOC Spares (pad retaining spring clip, front, 4-cylinder)

brakes.front.pad-clip.notes: Pressed down while the split pins are drawn (Sec 10 para 2).

brakes.front.plug.name: Caliper plug
brakes.front.plug.notes: Blanks the bleed hole not used on this side (the halves are cast alike).

specs.label: Thread
specs.ref: As the bleed screw it replaces

brakes.front.caliper-bolt.name: Caliper securing bolt
brakes.front.caliper-bolt.notes: Two per caliper, from behind the swivel axle's caliper flange into the lugs, under the tab washer (Sec 11 para 2). 7/16 UNF x 1 1/4 derived.

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Tab, swivel axle flange and lug

brakes.front.hose.name: Front flexible hose
brakes.front.hose.notes: From the bracket on the body to the caliper union (Sec 8 paras 2-3): the top end's hex under the bracket, held by the locking plate, shakeproof washer and nut, the pipe's union nut screwed into it; the bottom end screwed into the caliper on a copper washer. Run and length derived for the static ride height and straight-ahead steering; P9 checks lock and bump.

brakes.front.hose-bracket-lh.name: Front hose bracket, LH
brakes.front.hose-bracket-lh.notes: Pressed bracket on the wing valance (P11 builds the valance it is welded to): a shelf the hose end passes through, with the slot for the locking plate's tongue. Position derived (front_suspension_layout.HOSE_BRACKET).

brakes.handbrake.handle.name: Handbrake lever (handle)
brakes.handbrake.handle.notes: Flat steel lever on the right of the tunnel, pivoted at its rear end on the spigot welded through it, cranked up to the grip at the front; pulling it up swings the operating lever's lower end forward and draws the cable inner. The pawl pivots on its inner face, the pawl rod's guides on its outer face. Shape from Fig 9.10; length and position derived (the seats and tunnel are P11).

specs.label: Thickness
specs.ref: In the plane of the ratchet sector

brakes.handbrake.ratchet-plate.name: Ratchet plate
brakes.handbrake.ratchet-plate.notes: Bolted to the tunnel wall by three bolts (Sec 16 para 3), carrying the toothed sector and the spigot's bush through the wall.

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Into caged nuts in the tunnel (P11)

brakes.handbrake.operating-lever.name: Operating lever
brakes.handbrake.operating-lever.notes: On the spigot's squared end inside the tunnel, its forked lower end carrying the trunnion under the floor line (Sec 4 para 2).

brakes.handbrake.adjusting-nut.name: Cable adjusting nut (brass)
brakes.handbrake.adjusting-nut.notes: Turned to adjust the cable until the shoes lock at 4 or 5 notches (Sec 4 para 2).

brakes.handbrake.cable.name: Handbrake cable (outer)

partNumbers.by: MGOC Spares (cable, handbrake, banjo axle, wire wheels)

brakes.handbrake.cable.notes: From the front abutment A under the floor back beside the tunnel, up the heel board ahead of the axle, over the right-hand tube (clip 29) and behind the banjo bowl to the outer compensating lever (Fig 9.10; MGOC: the early cable is secured at the rear of the differential). Grease nipple not modelled (Sec 2 para 5). Route derived.

brakes.handbrake.cable-inner.name: Handbrake cable (inner, exposed ends)
brakes.handbrake.cable-inner.notes: The threaded front end through the trunnion and the rear end across the compensator's tabs.

brakes.handbrake.comp-lever-inner.name: Inner compensating lever
brakes.handbrake.comp-lever-inner.notes: On P7's fulcrum pin on the rear of the bowl; its tip pulls the left-hand rod, its tab takes the cable inner's end; the outer lever's tab takes the outer's ferrule, so the cable closes the two tabs and the levers pull both rods (scissor compensator). Shapes from Fig 9.10; sizes derived.

brakes.handbrake.rod-lh.name: Handbrake rod, LH
brakes.handbrake.rod-lh.notes: From the inner compensating lever's tip to the lever on the LH backplate, forked at both ends with a locknut at the wheel end (Sec 16 para 6). Length derived.

brakes.handbrake.rod-rh.name: Handbrake rod, RH
brakes.handbrake.rod-rh.notes: From the outer lever's tip behind the bowl to the RH backplate lever.

brakes.lines.four-way.name: Four-way connection
brakes.lines.four-way.notes: Forged block on its spacer on the bulkhead below the pedal box, bolted through the middle (Fig 9.1 items 5-6): the master cylinder pipe into the top, the stop lamp switch beside it, the front pipes out of each side and the rear pipe out of the bottom. Position derived: under the box, clear of the pedals where they cross the bulkhead and of the clutch hose. Shape after Fig 9.1.

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Block, spacer, 1 mm bulkhead panel and nut

brakes.lines.four-way-nut.name: Four-way connection nut
brakes.lines.four-way-nut.notes: On the footwell side of the bulkhead (P11 builds the panel; 1 mm assumed).

brakes.lines.stop-switch.name: Stop lamp switch (hydraulic)
brakes.lines.stop-switch.notes: Pressure switch screwed into the four-way connection (Fig 9.1 item 7; item 8 is the alternative design). Two spade terminals for the stop lamp feed (P10).

brakes.lines.mc-pipe.name: Pipe, master cylinder to four-way connection
brakes.lines.mc-pipe.notes: Brazed into the banjo (parts/brakes/master.py), down through the grommet in the pedal box floor, back under the box outboard of the brake pedal and down to the connection; tube nut at the connection. Route derived.

specs.label: Outside diameter
specs.ref: 3/16 in brake pipe, as the clutch pipe; not in Haynes

specs.label: Outside diameter
specs.ref: 13 mm hole in the box floor

brakes.lines.front-pipe-lh.name: Pipe, four-way connection to LH front hose
brakes.lines.front-pipe-lh.notes: Up the bulkhead face beside the pedal box, across above the bellhousing, down the left side and forward along the chassis leg, up and out to the hose bracket on the wing valance, its nut in the hose end (Sec 8 para 2). Route derived; P11 clips it to the bulkhead and leg, P9 checks it against the suspension.

brakes.lines.front-pipe-rh.name: Pipe, four-way connection to RH front hose
brakes.lines.front-pipe-rh.notes: Outboard to the right chassis leg, forward along it and up and out to the hose bracket. Route derived.

brakes.lines.rear-pipe.name: Pipe, four-way connection to rear hose
brakes.lines.rear-pipe.notes: Down the toe board, back under the floor beside the tunnel on the right, rising ahead of the axle to the rear hose bracket. Route derived (P11: floor clips).

brakes.lines.rear-hose-bracket.name: Rear hose bracket (on the body)
brakes.lines.rear-hose-bracket.notes: Shelf the rear hose's top end passes through, welded to the body ahead of and above the axle (P11). Position derived.

brakes.lines.rear-hose.name: Rear flexible hose
brakes.lines.rear-hose.notes: From the body bracket down and back to the three-way connection on the axle, slack for the axle's travel. Length and run derived.

specs.label: Outside diameter
specs.ref: Brake hose, as the front ones

brakes.lines.union.name: Three-way connection (axle)
brakes.lines.union.notes: On the tab on top of the right-hand neck of the axle case (rear_axle_layout.PIPE_BRACKET; Figs 9.1-9.3 draw it right of the differential): the hose into the top, the two axle pipes from its sides; the ear bolted to the tab. Fig 9.1 shows a separate bracket (10) on later axles; on the banjo axle the case carries the tab.

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Ear and washer into the tapped tab

brakes.lines.axle-pipe-lh.name: Axle pipe, LH
brakes.lines.axle-pipe-lh.notes: From the three-way connection behind the banjo bowl (above the filler plug and clear of the handbrake compensator), along the rear-upper side of the left tube, over to the front by the backplate and down to the wheel cylinder's inlet behind the backplate. P9: the U-bolts pass outside it. Route derived.

brakes.lines.axle-clip.name: Axle pipe clip
brakes.lines.axle-clip.notes: One on each tube between the union and the spring seat.

brakes.master.mc-body.name: Brake master cylinder and supply tank
brakes.master.mc-body.notes: Cast cylinder with a two-bolt flange on the pedal box's mounting wall beside the clutch cylinder (outboard of it on RHD cars, photo 1.1), the square pressed-steel supply tank over its forward part with the filler neck on top, and the outlet boss through the tank's front face for the banjo connector. Feed and by-pass (compensating) ports from the tank into the bore (Sec 18 para 2: probe the compensating hole). Keep the fluid 1/4 in below the bottom of the filler neck (Sec 2 para 2). Shape from Fig 9.11 and photo 1.1; tank and casting sizes derived in proportion to the 3/4 in bore.

specs.label: Tank width
specs.ref: Fig 9.11 and photo 1.1, in proportion to the bore

brakes.master.mc-cap.name: Supply tank cap
brakes.master.mc-cap.notes: Fluted cap with its breather hole (Sec 2 para 2).

brakes.master.valve.name: Valve assembly
brakes.master.valve.notes: In the large end of the return spring, at the outlet end of the bore (Sec 18 para 4).

brakes.master.spring-retainer.name: Spring retainer
brakes.master.spring-retainer.notes: In the small end of the spring, against the main cup (Sec 18 para 4). Form as the clutch cylinder's.

brakes.master.main-cup.name: Main cup
brakes.master.main-cup.notes: Fitted lip end first, pressed against the spring retainer (Sec 18 para 4).

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: As the clutch cylinder's main cup (same 3/4 in bore)

brakes.master.piston-washer.name: Piston washer
brakes.master.piston-washer.notes: Concave face against the main cup (Sec 18 para 4).

brakes.master.secondary-cup.name: Secondary cup
brakes.master.secondary-cup.notes: In the groove in the piston, lip toward the piston head (Sec 18 para 3).

brakes.master.pushrod.name: Pushrod
brakes.master.pushrod.notes: With the stop washer under the circlip and the clevis fork on its locknut; the fork takes the brake pedal's clevis pin (Sec 17 para 3).

brakes.master.banjo.name: Banjo connector
brakes.master.banjo.notes: On the outlet boss, its stub pointing down; the pipe to the four-way connection is brazed in (Fig 9.1 item 1).

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Two gaskets and the banjo into the outlet boss

brakes.master.mc-bolt-long.name: Master cylinder bolt (top, long)
brakes.master.mc-bolt-long.notes: The longer bolt goes in the top hole (Sec 17 para 5), through the flange and the mounting wall; nut and spring washer inside the box.

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Flange, wall, washer, nut and a little more than the short bolt

specs.label: Thread
specs.ref: 5/16 in UNF, as the clutch cylinder's fixings

brakes.master.pedal-box.name: Pedal box (master cylinder box)
brakes.master.pedal-box.notes: Pressed steel box on the engine side of the bulkhead (photo 1.1): the rear section the clutch and brake pedals hang in, open underneath, the common pivot bolt through its side walls (Sec 24 para 3); the mounting wall carrying both master cylinders (spigot and bolt holes, and a hole the clutch pipe passes); the front section round the cylinders with a floor (grommet hole for the brake pipe), a front wall and a rim the protecting cover screws to; a flange round its rear edge on the bulkhead with six bolt holes (Sec 19 para 7, later box); the anchor bar inside the rear flange with tabs for the two pedal pull-off springs. Form from Fig 9.16 item 11 and photo 1.1; every size and position derived (mgb/brake_layout.py). P11 builds the bulkhead it bolts to and the toe board slots the pedals pass through.

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Bulkhead to clear of the clutch cylinder's banjo bolt

brakes.master.cover.name: Master cylinder protecting cover

chassis.rear.pedestal.name: Bump rubber pedestal
chassis.rear.pedestal.notes: Saddle on the tube top (P7 PEDESTAL_SEAT) clamped by the U-bolts, thick under their lifted crown with a channel for the axle brake pipe (D, to suit P8's pipe route), two arched webs up to the platform for the bump rubber.

chassis.rear.bump-rubber.name: Bump rubber
chassis.rear.bump-rubber.notes: Strikes the body above (P11: rear_suspension_layout BUMP_STRIKE). Static gap derived.

specs.label: Diameter
specs.ref: Fig 11.4 proportions, inside the pedestal's lip

chassis.rear.damper-bracket.name: Hydraulic shock absorber attachment bracket
chassis.rear.damper-bracket.notes: Plate under the lower locating plate on the U-bolts, its inboard web carrying the stud for the damper link (Sec 8 para 1, Sec 10 para 1). Form derived from Fig 11.4.

chassis.rear.eye-bush.name: Bush (front eye)
chassis.rear.eye-bush.notes: Pressed into the front eye (Sec 8 para 3); steel inner sleeve on the eyebolt. Eye bore 1 1/8 in (D).

chassis.rear.eyebolt.name: Eyebolt
chassis.rear.eyebolt.notes: Through the front hanger (P11: rear_suspension_layout FRONT_HANGER) and the eye bush. 1/2 UNF (D).

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Spring width, bush flanges, hanger plates, washer and nut

chassis.rear.shackle-pin-plate.name: Shackle and pin plate
chassis.rear.shackle-pin-plate.notes: Inner plate with two pins welded in, through the spring's rear eye and the body bracket (P11: SHACKLE_BRACKET); tap each pin out in turn (Sec 8 para 1). Shackle length 3 1/2 in (D).

chassis.rear.shackle-bush.name: Shackle rubber bush
chassis.rear.shackle-bush.notes: Top-hat halves, one from each side of the spring eye and of the body bracket's eye.

chassis.rear.damper.name: Rear hydraulic damper (lever arm)
chassis.rear.damper.notes: Armstrong lever-arm unit on the body side member ahead of the axle (Sec 10 para 1; filler topped up through the access grommet behind the seats, photo 2.4): the cast body, the piston bore across it with hexagon end caps, the lid and filler plug, the mounting flange with two bolt lugs, the arm on its shaft pointing rearward to the link. Keep upright off the car. Body size from Fig 11.5 proportions. P11 builds the side member face (DAMPER_MOUNT).

specs.label: Arm centres
specs.note: Shock absorber arm centres, rear 5 1/4 in (133 mm)

chassis.rear.link.name: Damper link
chassis.rear.link.notes: Rod with rubber-bushed eyes from the damper arm to the bracket's stud (Fig 11.5); MGOC: chrome and rubber bumper links are not interchangeable.

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Flange, side member, washers and nut

chassis.rear.rebound-strap.name: Rebound strap
chassis.rear.rebound-strap.notes: Check strap from the body bolt (P11: REBOUND_BOLT) to the axle's spindle (P7 REBOUND_EYE), leaning back so it clears the tube; the spindle nut (item 26) is the axle's. Section derived.

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Tube, body bracket, washers and nut

chassis.steering.rack-housing.name: Rack housing
chassis.steering.rack-housing.notes: Tube with the pinion housing cast on its right-hand end at the column's angle (RHD), the damper (yoke) boss under it opposite the pinion with its cover, the pinion end cover flange, the lubricator boss (Sec 2 para 3: ten strokes of the gun) and two flat pads the mounting brackets clamp on. Bare casting (D). Rack bush (75) and its screw (74) inside the left-hand end are not drawn.

chassis.steering.rack.name: Rack
chassis.steering.rack.notes: Bar with its teeth on top under the pinion; pulled out from the pinion end (Sec 26 para 2). Diameter and tooth pitch derived.

chassis.steering.pinion.name: Pinion
chassis.steering.pinion.notes: Helical teeth meshing on the rack's top; splined top with the cut-out the joint's pinch bolt passes through (Sec 17 para 3). On one axis with the column (Sec 20, Fig 11.8). Tooth count derived.

specs.label: Nut torque
specs.note: Steering rack and pinion bearing nut

chassis.steering.damper-cover.name: Damper cover
chassis.steering.damper-cover.notes: Closes the yoke boss; shims (8) and joint (9) under it set the yoke's clearance (Sec 26).

chassis.steering.yoke.name: Yoke
chassis.steering.yoke.notes: Presses the rack against the pinion; its pad (6) and spring (7) are inside it (not drawn).

chassis.steering.bracket.name: Rack mounting bracket
chassis.steering.bracket.notes: Strap over the housing's pad, a foot each side bolted down into the crossmember boss (Sec 20 para 6).

chassis.steering.shim.name: Rack shim
chassis.steering.shim.notes: Between the bracket and the crossmember boss to line the pinion up with the column, riveted to the boss when right (Sec 20 para 6 b-f). One drawn each side.

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Bracket foot, shim and the boss's tapped hole

chassis.steering.ball-housing.name: Ball housing
chassis.steering.ball-housing.notes: Screws on the rack end over the tie-rod's ball, ball seat (23) and spring (24); locked by the special locknut (26) whose tabs are punched into the rack's slots (Sec 26 para 2).

chassis.steering.tie-rod.name: Tie-rod
chassis.steering.tie-rod.notes: Inner ball in the ball housing, the outer end threaded for the ball joint; toe-in is set by turning both rods equally (Sec 11).

chassis.steering.outer-joint.name: Outer balljoint assembly
chassis.steering.outer-joint.notes: Forged body with its socket under the steering lever, the ball pin up through the lever's taper, the boot (31) with its retainer (32) and garter spring (33); cannot be repaired (Sec 12 para 1).

chassis.steering.joint-nut.name: Balljoint nut (self-locking)
chassis.steering.joint-nut.notes: Use a new self-locking nut (Sec 12 para 2).

chassis.steering.joint-washer.name: Balljoint plain washer (early levers)
chassis.steering.joint-washer.notes: Early production cars have a plain washer under the balljoint nut (Sec 12 para 2).

chassis.steering.uj-yoke.name: Universal joint yoke
chassis.steering.uj-yoke.notes: Split splined boss with a pinch bolt across it; the bolt passes through the cut-out in the shaft's splines (Sec 17 para 3). Early joint overhauled like the propeller shaft joints (Sec 17 para 2).

chassis.steering.outer-tube.name: Column outer tube, RHD
chassis.steering.outer-tube.notes: Through the toe board and the RHD crossmember's column tube (D) to under the wheel.

chassis.steering.upper-bearing.name: Column upper bearing
chassis.steering.upper-bearing.notes: Nylon bush between the columns (Sec 19 para 2); the felt bush (55) is used with a steering lock and is not fitted.

chassis.steering.column-clamp.name: Steering column clamp
chassis.steering.column-clamp.notes: Round the outer tube, its top plate to the body bracket under the facia with packing washers (P11: steering_layout COLUMN_TOP_CLAMP; Sec 20 paras 5-7).

chassis.steering.bottom-bracket.name: Steering column bottom bracket
chassis.steering.bottom-bracket.notes: On the toe board round the tube (P11: steering_layout COLUMN_TOE_PLATE), with the blanking plate (66), nuts and washers.

chassis.steering.wheel.name: Steering wheel (16 1/2 in banjo)
chassis.steering.wheel.notes: Early wheel with an integral boss (Sec 18 para 2): acetate rim with finger grips, three banjo spokes of four spring-steel wires each (MGOC: three-spoke banjo wheel; four wires per spoke D from the banjo pattern), the black hub boss. Spokes set in a T with the wheels straight ahead (D). Dish derived.

chassis.steering.horn-push.name: Horn push with MG badge
chassis.steering.horn-push.notes: Central horn push carrying the MG badge - silver letters and octagon on red wavy lines (MGOC); drawn with the octagon bezel and the letters as raised blocks. The horn contact is P10.

clutch.hydraulics.mc-body.name: Master cylinder and reservoir
clutch.hydraulics.mc-body.notes: Cast iron body (Moss Motors 180-697) with an integral round reservoir beside the two-bolt flange, bolted to the front of the pedal box on the right-hand side of the bulkhead beside the brake master cylinder; a cover over both is held by four screws (Sec 5 para 1). The outlet at the front takes the banjo and banjo bolt (items 32-33). Feed and by-pass ports drilled from the reservoir well (Sec 5 para 6: probe the by-pass ports). Shape from Fig 5.3; sizes in proportion to the published bore.

specs.label: Bore
specs.note: MGB 1962-80 clutch master cylinder, 3/4 in bore

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Fig 5.3, in proportion to the bore

clutch.hydraulics.mc-cap.name: Master cylinder cap
clutch.hydraulics.mc-cap.notes: Fluted filler cap with a breather hole. Refit after topping up (Sec 3 para 5); do not overfill (Sec 2).

specs.label: Diameter
specs.ref: Fig 5.3, in proportion to the reservoir

clutch.hydraulics.mc-boot.name: Master cylinder boot
clutch.hydraulics.mc-boot.notes: Pull off to dismantle (Sec 5 para 5). Fluid in the boot means a leaking seal (Sec 9 para 14).

clutch.hydraulics.mc-circlip.name: Master cylinder circlip
clutch.hydraulics.mc-circlip.notes: Press the pushrod in and remove the circlip to withdraw the internals (Sec 5 para 5).

specs.label: Outside diameter
specs.ref: Internal circlip in the bore mouth

clutch.hydraulics.mc-pushrod.name: Master cylinder pushrod
clutch.hydraulics.mc-pushrod.notes: Pushrod with its stop washer, threaded into the clevis fork with a locknut; the fork takes the clevis pin through the pedal (Sec 5 para 3).

specs.label: Diameter
specs.ref: Fig 5.3, in proportion to the bore

clutch.hydraulics.mc-secondary-cup.name: Secondary cup
clutch.hydraulics.mc-secondary-cup.notes: Fitted over the piston, fully home in its groove, lip toward the cylinder bore (Sec 5 para 8).

specs.label: Diameter
specs.ref: Running fit in the 3/4 in bore

clutch.hydraulics.mc-piston-washer.name: Piston washer
clutch.hydraulics.mc-piston-washer.notes: Between the piston head and the main cup (Sec 5 para 9).

clutch.hydraulics.mc-main-cup.name: Main cup
clutch.hydraulics.mc-main-cup.notes: Fitted lip edge first, after the spring (Sec 5 para 9).

clutch.hydraulics.mc-spring-retainer.name: Spring retainer
clutch.hydraulics.mc-spring-retainer.notes: Fitted in the small end of the spring (Sec 5 para 8).

clutch.hydraulics.mc-spring.name: Master cylinder spring
clutch.hydraulics.mc-spring.notes: Fitted large end first (Sec 5 para 9). Modelled as a parallel coil.

clutch.hydraulics.mc-bolt-long.name: Master cylinder securing bolt (top, long)
clutch.hydraulics.mc-bolt-long.notes: The longer bolt goes in the top hole, which also carries the stiffener plate (Sec 5 para 11).

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Flange, box wall, stiffener, washer and nut

clutch.hydraulics.mc-bolt.name: Master cylinder securing bolt (bottom)
clutch.hydraulics.mc-bolt.notes: Sec 5 para 4: two securing bolts, nuts and washers.

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Flange, box wall, washer and nut

specs.label: Thread diameter
specs.ref: 5/16 in UNF, matching the flange holes

clutch.hydraulics.mc-stiffener.name: Master cylinder stiffener plate
clutch.hydraulics.mc-stiffener.notes: Carried by the top bolt (Sec 5 para 11). Fitted inside the pedal box under the nut; Haynes does not draw it, so its shape is derived.

clutch.hydraulics.banjo.name: Banjo connection
clutch.hydraulics.banjo.notes: Banjo eye on the master cylinder outlet with the metal pipe brazed in. Undo the union at the master cylinder to remove it (Sec 5 para 3).

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Through two washers and the banjo into the outlet boss

clutch.hydraulics.metal-pipe.name: Metal pipe (RHD)
clutch.hydraulics.metal-pipe.notes: RHD pipe from the master cylinder banjo down the bulkhead to the hose at its bracket (Fig 5.3 inset), with its union nut. Run derived: Fig 5.3 shows it dropping from the master cylinder to the bracket; the bracket position is in mgb/clutch_layout.py.

specs.label: Outside diameter
specs.ref: 3/16 in brake pipe, the usual size for these systems; not in Haynes

clutch.hydraulics.pipe-clip.name: Pipe clip
clutch.hydraulics.pipe-clip.notes: Two P-clips holding the pipe (items 30 and 31 are the same clip in two places).

clutch.hydraulics.hose.name: Flexible hose
clutch.hydraulics.hose.notes: From the bracket, where its top end is held by a locknut and lockwasher and the pipe screws into it, to the slave cylinder union. Disconnect at the cylinder to remove the slave cylinder (Sec 6 para 1). End fittings are crimped on.

specs.label: Across flats
specs.ref: Fig 5.3, to the hose end thread

clutch.hydraulics.slave-body.name: Slave cylinder body
clutch.hydraulics.slave-body.notes: On the right-hand side of the bellhousing, held by two bolts and spring washers (Sec 6 para 1). Domed closed end with the hose union and the bleed screw boss; the two-ear flange is at the open end, on the rear face of the bellhousing pad, and the body passes forward through the pad (mgb/gearbox_layout.py). Lockheed type, MGB 1962-80 (Moss Motors 180-720, GSY106). Shape from Fig 5.3.

specs.label: Bore
specs.ref: 1 in, as commonly quoted for the GSY106 cylinder; no published figure could be confirmed

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Fig 5.3, in proportion to the bore

clutch.hydraulics.slave-boot.name: Slave cylinder boot
clutch.hydraulics.slave-boot.notes: Remove the boot and shake out the internals to dismantle (Sec 6 para 2).

clutch.hydraulics.slave-pushrod.name: Slave cylinder pushrod
clutch.hydraulics.slave-pushrod.notes: Stays on the clutch release fork when the cylinder is pulled off (Sec 6 para 1).

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Through the lever fork and the pushrod eye

clutch.hydraulics.bleed-screw.name: Bleed screw
clutch.hydraulics.bleed-screw.notes: Open one turn with a 9 in tube over it into a jar to bleed; tighten at the end of a downstroke (Sec 3 paras 2-4).

clutch.hydraulics.bleed-cap.name: Bleed screw dust cap
clutch.hydraulics.bleed-cap.notes: Sec 3 para 3: remove the dust cap before opening the bleed screw.

clutch.hydraulics.slave-bolt.name: Slave cylinder bolt
clutch.hydraulics.slave-bolt.notes: Sec 6 para 1: two bolts and spring washers. MGOC Spares SH605071, 5/16 in UNF x 7/8 in.

specs.label: Length
specs.note: SH605071 screw, hex head, 5/16 in UNF x 7/8 in

clutch.hydraulics.slave-spring-washer.name: Slave cylinder bolt spring washer
clutch.hydraulics.slave-spring-washer.notes: MGOC Spares GHF332, 5/16 in spring washer.

clutch.pedal.pedal.name: Clutch pedal
clutch.pedal.pedal.notes: Pressed-steel pedal hung from the pivot in the pedal box, the master cylinder pushrod clevis just below the pivot, the arm cranked back through the bulkhead to the foot plate (Fig 5.3). RHD: the clutch pedal is the inboard of the two. Shape from Fig 5.3; lengths and the pad position derived (mgb/clutch_layout.py).

specs.label: Pivot to pad
specs.ref: Pivot to pad centre in the layout

clutch.pedal.pad.name: Pedal rubber pad
clutch.pedal.pad.notes: Ribbed rubber pad stretched over the foot plate (Fig 5.3).

clutch.pedal.distance-tube.name: Distance tube
clutch.pedal.distance-tube.notes: Runs on the pivot bolt inside the bush (Sec 8 para 5 calls it the spacer).

clutch.pedal.return-spring.name: Pedal return spring
clutch.pedal.return-spring.notes: Hooked from the pedal arm to the pedal box (Sec 8 para 4, "free the spring"). Anchor point derived.

clutch.pedal.clevis-pin.name: Pedal clevis pin
clutch.pedal.clevis-pin.notes: Joins the master cylinder pushrod fork to the pedal; free it by removing the split pin (Sec 5 para 3).

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Through the fork and the pedal

clutch.release.carbon.name: Release bearing (graphite ring)
clutch.release.carbon.notes: Graphite ring pressed into its cup; it runs against the release plate (Fig 5.2). Renew it at every clutch overhaul unless nearly new (Sec 4 para 4, Sec 7 para 1; photo 7.1a worn, 7.1b unworn). Radii and length from Fig 5.2, scaled.

clutch.release.cup.name: Release bearing cup
clutch.release.cup.notes: Pressed cup holding the graphite ring, with a lug and trunnion pin at 12 and 6 o'clock that the lever fork sits on (Fig 5.1 item 8 draws the lug and pin; photo 7.1b shows the cup in the fork with the clips either side).

clutch.release.clip.name: Bearing retainer clip
clutch.release.clip.notes: Turn the clips through 90 degrees and remove them to free the bearing (Sec 4 para 5, Sec 7 para 2). MGOC Spares 22B66.

clutch.release.lever.name: Clutch withdrawal lever
clutch.release.lever.notes: Forged lever pivoted on a bolt in the gearbox front cover (photo 7.3; mgaguru.com gt110). A half-ring fork carries the bearing on its two trunnions; the outer arm passes out through the bellhousing wall under the dust cover to the slave cylinder pushrod. Check for play and have the bushes renewed if necessary (Sec 7 para 3). The early three-synchro lever differs from the four-synchro one (MGOC Spares 22B57). Shape and lever ratio derived: Haynes has no drawing of the lever; positions from mgb/gearbox_layout.py.

specs.label: Fork thickness
specs.ref: In proportion to the 3/8 in pivot bolt

specs.label: Ratio
specs.ref: Pivot to pushrod line 130 mm over pivot to trunnions 75 mm

specs.label: Outside diameter
specs.ref: Bronze bush over the 3/8 in bolt

specs.label: Inside diameter
specs.ref: Running fit on the 3/8 in pivot bolt

clutch.release.pivot-bolt.name: Withdrawal lever pivot bolt
clutch.release.pivot-bolt.notes: Sec 7 para 3: remove the locknut, washer and bolt (photo 7.3). MGOC Spares 11G3196.

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Through both lugs and the lever boss, washer and locknut

specs.label: Thread diameter
specs.note: Lever fittings: GHF223 nyloc nut, 3/8 in UNF

clutch.release.locknut.name: Pivot bolt locknut
clutch.release.locknut.notes: Self-locking nut, 3/8 in UNF (MGOC Spares GHF223).

clutch.release.dust-cover.name: Withdrawal lever dust cover
clutch.release.dust-cover.notes: Rubber gaiter over the lever's opening in the bellhousing (Sec 7 para 3, "disengage the dust cover"). Oval section on chrome bumper cars (MGOC Spares 22H1337). Shape derived: flange, two convolutions and a neck on the lever.

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Wall to the neck on the lever

clutch.unit.cover.name: Clutch cover with straps and fulcrum rivets
clutch.unit.cover.notes: Deep pressed dish with three bolting lobes, each carrying two of the six cover screws and one of the three locating dowels (Sec 4 paras 2-3 and 11; photo 4.11 shows the dowel beside a screw on a lobe). The skirt has windows the pressure plate lugs pass through; the three drive straps are riveted outside on raised pads and bolted to the lugs (Fig 5.1 shows them on the outside of the cover; Sec 4 para 5 reaches the strap bolts "through the holes in the cover"). A pressed bead in the back wall carries the nine shouldered fulcrum rivets (the round buttons drawn in Fig 5.1) and the two wire fulcrum rings either side of the diaphragm (Fig 5.2). Balance holes in the back wall (Fig 5.1). Mark the cover and flywheel before removal (Sec 4 para 2). Shape from Figs 5.1 and 5.2 and photo 4.11; depths from Fig 5.2. No photograph of a bare early cover could be viewed from the sandbox.

specs.label: Depth
specs.ref: Fig 5.2: flywheel face to the back of the cover, scaled to the 8 in plate

specs.label: Flange diameter
specs.ref: Fig 5.2: lobe tips at 137-138 mm radius, scaled

specs.label: Screws
specs.note: Sec 4 para 2: six bolts holding the cover to the flywheel

clutch.unit.diaphragm-spring.name: Diaphragm spring
clutch.unit.diaphragm-spring.notes: Dished spring steel diaphragm: its rim bears on the pressure plate's fulcrum ridge, it pivots between the two wire rings on the cover rivets, and the eighteen fingers carry the release plate (Fig 5.2). The finger slots end in round holes on the pivot circle, every other one taking a rivet. Finger count from Fig 5.1; radii from Fig 5.2.

specs.label: Outside diameter
specs.ref: Fig 5.2, scaled: rim just outside the fulcrum ridge

clutch.unit.release-plate.name: Release plate
clutch.unit.release-plate.notes: Early models only (Sec 4 para 5): a cast plate on the diaphragm finger tips that the graphite release bearing runs against. Its spigot passes through the diaphragm and is held by a circlip; three spring straps hold it to the cover (Fig 5.2 item 8). Shape from Fig 5.2.

specs.label: Diameter
specs.ref: Fig 5.2, scaled: on the finger tips inside the cover opening

clutch.unit.release-plate-circlip.name: Release plate circlip
clutch.unit.release-plate-circlip.notes: Sec 4 para 5: remove the circlip holding the release plate in position (early models only).

specs.label: Inside diameter
specs.ref: Sprung into the groove on the release plate spigot

clutch.unit.release-plate-strap.name: Strap, release plate to cover
clutch.unit.release-plate-strap.notes: Thin spring strap riveted between an ear of the release plate and the cover bead (Fig 5.2 item 8).

clutch.unit.pressure-plate.name: Pressure plate
clutch.unit.pressure-plate.notes: Cast iron ring with the machined friction face, the fulcrum ridge on its back for the diaphragm rim, three drilled lugs for the strap bolts and a ring of cast balance lugs round the back (Fig 5.1). Check the face for grooves and cracks (Sec 4 para 7).

specs.label: Outside diameter
specs.ref: Fig 5.2, scaled, then held inside the cover skirt so the cover screw heads clear it

clutch.unit.pressure-plate-clip.name: Pressure plate clip
clutch.unit.pressure-plate-clip.notes: Under each strap bolt; its hooked end goes over the diaphragm rim so the pressure plate is drawn back with it when the clutch is released (Fig 5.2 item 4). Shape from Fig 5.1 item 5.

specs.label: Width
specs.ref: Fig 5.1, in proportion to the strap bolt

clutch.unit.strap-bolt.name: Strap bolt
clutch.unit.strap-bolt.notes: Sec 4 para 5: undo the three strap bolts a turn at a time through the holes in the cover.

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Through the tab washer, strap and clip into the lug

clutch.unit.cover-screw.name: Cover assembly retaining screw
clutch.unit.cover-screw.notes: Unscrew diagonally half a turn at a time to avoid distorting the cover flange (Sec 4 para 2); tighten to the specified torque in a diagonal sequence (para 13).

specs.label: Thread diameter
specs.ref: 5/16 in, to the flywheel's tapped holes; not in Haynes

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Lobe, spring washer and thread into the flywheel

clutch.unit.hub.name: Driven plate hub
clutch.unit.hub.notes: Splined hub and flange of the driven plate. The shorter end faces the flywheel; the plate is marked FLYWHEEL SIDE (Sec 4 para 10). Centralise it on an old first motion shaft (photo 4.12). Lengths each side of the plate from Fig 5.2.

specs.label: Splines
specs.note: Clutch alignment tool GAC5057 for MGA 1600 and MGB to 1965 (three-bearing): 23 splines

specs.label: Spline major diameter
specs.ref: 1 in nominal, in proportion to the hub in Fig 5.2; not published

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Fig 5.2, scaled: 9 mm ahead of the plate, 24 mm behind

clutch.unit.carrier.name: Driven plate centre (side plates, cushion segments, rivets)
clutch.unit.carrier.notes: Front side plate carrying twelve waved cushion segments, the rear retainer plate, six stop pins through notches in the hub flange, and the facing rivets. Pressed louvres over the six spring windows (Fig 5.1, photo 4.3). Inspect for loose rivets, distortion and cracks (Sec 4 para 6).

specs.label: Segments
specs.ref: Typical Borg & Beck 8 in plate; Fig 5.1 shows the rivet pattern but not the segments

clutch.unit.damper-spring.name: Driven plate damper spring
clutch.unit.damper-spring.notes: Six damper springs, colour black/light green (p106). Seen in the cut-away of Fig 5.1 and in photo 4.3.

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Fig 5.1, in proportion to the hub

clutch.unit.facing.name: Driven plate facing
clutch.unit.facing.notes: Two riveted facings, counterbored so the rivet heads sit below the friction face. Rivet pattern from Fig 5.1: an outer ring and an inner ring of holes. Renew the plate complete rather than refacing it (Sec 4 para 6).

specs.label: Inside diameter
specs.ref: Fig 5.1: inner edge at 0.70 of the outer

cooling.pump-body.name: Water pump body
cooling.pump-body.notes: Centrifugal pump driven by the fan belt (Haynes p55). Held by four bolts with gaskets (Sec 9 para 5); the top plug takes grease on early cars (Sec 2 para 3). It bolts to the block in the notch at the top of the front plate.

specs.label: Inlet diameter
specs.ref: Takes the bottom hose; not published

cooling.pump-spindle.name: Water pump spindle, bearing and vane
cooling.pump-spindle.notes: Bearing assembly (item 3) located by the bearing wire (item 4); the vane (item 2) is pressed on the inner end.

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: From the vane to the pulley hub

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Through the flange into the block

specs.label: Torque
specs.note: Water pump to crankcase, early models

cooling.pump-pulley.name: Water pump pulley
cooling.pump-pulley.notes: MG part 12B174A for the 18G (MG Owners' Club Spares listing). In line with the crankshaft pulley groove.

cooling.fan.name: Cooling fan (three blade)
cooling.fan.notes: Three-blade metal fan, 12H1058, fitted from the earliest MGBs in 1962 (MG Owners' Club Spares, mechanical cooling fan listing). Belt-driven on the water pump pulley on early models (Haynes p55).

specs.label: Diameter
specs.ref: Inside the radiator core; not published

cooling.fan-belt.name: Fan belt
cooling.fan-belt.notes: Runs on the crankshaft, water pump and alternator pulleys; tension 1/2 in deflection at the middle of the longest run (Haynes p55).

specs.label: Deflection
specs.note: Haynes prints 12.8 mm for 1/2 in; the inch figure governs

cooling.radiator.name: Radiator
cooling.radiator.notes: Vertical-flow radiator with top and bottom tanks, a tube-and-fin core, side channels for its mounting, filler neck with overflow pipe and a drain tap boss (Figs 2.2, 2.4; photo 7.6(b)). System capacity 9.5 Imp pints on early models (Haynes p55).

cooling.pressure-cap.name: Radiator pressure cap
cooling.pressure-cap.notes: Rated at 7 lbf/in2 on early models (Haynes p55).

cooling.drain-tap.name: Radiator drain tap

Modelled as a BCI group 26 size, which owners report fits the MGB box (britishcarforum.com thread 18387, 'MGB battery box dimensions'), in the right-hand carrier (see the questions for Oliver), with taper posts, six vent plugs and its cell partitions showing on the case. Negative earth (needed for the 18ACR).

electrical.charging.drive-end-bracket.name: Alternator drive end bracket
electrical.charging.drive-end-bracket.notes: Die-cast front bracket carrying the sealed drive end bearing (item 10, circlip 11, O ring 12). Shape from Fig 10.3 and photo 3.3 (Ch 2): a front wall with spokes and large cooling openings round the bearing boss, a skirt back to the stator, a pivot lug on the engine side and the tapped adjusting lug below, and ears for the three through-bolts. The 18ACR replaced the dynamo on the same mountings: two pivot bolts above and the link below (Ch 10 Sec 6 para 1, Sec 15 para 2, Sec 20 para 2). Lug positions are derived from the pivot line and link (mgb/electrical_layout.py). Outside reference for the form: the MGOC Spares and Rimmer Bros 16/17/18ACR listings (photographs could not be opened from the build machine).

specs.label: Outside diameter
specs.ref: Stator diameter less the bracket step (Fig 10.3 proportion)

electrical.charging.stator.name: Alternator stator
electrical.charging.stator.notes: Laminated stator clamped between the brackets; the lamination stack shows round the outside (Fig 10.3).

specs.label: Outside diameter
specs.ref: Scaled from Fig 10.3 against the 2 3/4 in pulley (stator about 1.8 x the pulley)

electrical.charging.slip-ring-bracket.name: Alternator slip ring end bracket
electrical.charging.slip-ring-bracket.notes: Rear bracket with the slip ring end bearing (item 7), cooling slots round its back and the rear pivot lug (Fig 10.3: the lug at the top of item 4). The brush box, rectifier and regulator sit on it under the end cover (Sec 21 para 1).

electrical.charging.end-cover.name: Alternator end cover
electrical.charging.end-cover.notes: Moulded cover held by two screws (Sec 21 para 1), slotted for cooling air, with the opening for the terminal block.

electrical.charging.rotor.name: Alternator rotor, shaft and slip rings
electrical.charging.rotor.notes: Claw-pole rotor (items 8, 9) on its shaft with the slip rings (6) at the back; seen through the bracket openings.

specs.label: Length
specs.ref: Shaft from the slip ring bearing to the pulley nut

electrical.charging.fan.name: Alternator cooling fan
electrical.charging.fan.notes: Pressed fan between the pulley and the drive end bracket (photo 3.3, Ch 2). MGOC Spares lists the AC/ACR fan C37222.

specs.label: Diameter
specs.ref: Photo 3.3 (Ch 2): the fan a little smaller than the drive end bracket

electrical.charging.pulley.name: Alternator pulley
electrical.charging.pulley.notes: Single-groove pulley in line with the crankshaft and water pump pulleys (mgb/cooling_layout.py BELT_X).

electrical.charging.shaft-nut.name: Alternator shaft nut and spring washer

specs.ref: Slip ring end bracket ear to the drive end bracket ear

electrical.charging.terminal-plug.name: Alternator terminal plug and leads
electrical.charging.terminal-plug.notes: The terminal block pulled off first on removal (Sec 15 para 2). Two brown output leads and the brown/yellow warning lamp lead (Fig 10.27 colour code).

electrical.charging.rear-bracket.name: Alternator rear mounting bracket
electrical.charging.rear-bracket.notes: Bracket 14 of Fig 2.6, held by screw 16 and spring washer 15 to the threaded boss on the right of the block (P2 block, x 124), its ear carrying the rear pivot bolt 31 with spring washer 32 and nut 33. MGOC lists 12A526 (dynamo, 18G/GA/GB) and 12G1053 (alternator); the ALT1 kit adapts a dynamo car. Shape derived from Fig 2.6.

specs.label: Thickness
specs.ref: Fig 2.6 proportion, against the 5/16 in screw

electrical.charging.link.name: Alternator adjusting link
electrical.charging.link.notes: Slotted link on the stud (17) with washer 26, spring washer 27 and nut 28; the link screw 29 and spring washer 30 into the alternator's adjusting lug. The slot is struck about the pivot line so the alternator swings to tension the belt (1/2 in deflection, Ch 2 p55).

electrical.charging.link-stud.name: Adjusting link stud (pillar)
electrical.charging.link-stud.notes: Stud 17 with its spring washer and nut (18, 19), screwed into the engine front through the front plate just outboard of the timing cover.

specs.ref: 9/16 in hexagon over the 5/16 in thread

electrical.charging.pivot-bolt.name: Alternator pivot bolt
electrical.charging.pivot-bolt.notes: Bolts 34 (front, through the water pump ear) and 31 (rear, through the bracket). MGOC: 5/16 UNF x 1 1/2 GHF104.

specs.ref: MGOC Spares GHF104 bolt 5/16 UNF x 1 1/2

electrical.coil.coil.name: Ignition coil, Lucas HA12

partNumbers.by: BP Northwest (GCL110MGB, 1963-74; 3 ohm primary with external ballast on later cars)

electrical.coil.coil.notes: Oil-filled can coil with a moulded cap: HT tower in the centre, SW (+) and CB (-) terminals either side. On the early cars it is on the engine, above the starter: Haynes removes the oil filter, the ignition coil and the coil attachment bracket before the starter (Ch 10 Sec 25 para 2). Its exact place - on the block's threaded boss between the oil filter and the dipstick - is derived (D). Can size from the common HA12 can (outside photographs could not be opened from the build machine).

specs.label: Height
specs.ref: Can 128 mm plus the cap and HT tower

electrical.coil.clamp.name: Coil clamp bracket
electrical.coil.clamp.notes: The 'coil attachment bracket' (Sec 25 para 2): band and pinch screw round the can, arm bolted to the block boss (P2 block, x 67). Form derived.

specs.label: Thread
specs.ref: 5/16 in into the block boss, as the alternator bracket

electrical.coil.king-lead.name: Coil HT (king) lead
electrical.coil.king-lead.notes: From the coil tower to the centre of the distributor cap (P3 distributor). Route derived.

specs.label: Diameter
specs.ref: 7 mm HT lead, as the plug leads (P3)

electrical.control.control-box.name: Control box, Lucas RB340
electrical.control.control-box.notes: Cut-out relay and the current and voltage regulators under a clipped cover (Fig 10.2, Sec 8). MGOC Spares: GEU6605, fitted to dynamo cars to 1967, 'mounted on the right-hand side of the engine bay, beside the fuse box'. With the 18ACR conversion the alternator's own regulator does the work; conversions usually leave the RB340 in place as a junction with its A and A1 (B) leads joined - see the questions for Oliver. Shape from Fig 10.2.

electrical.control.fuse-block.name: Fuse block, Lucas 4FJ (two fuses)
electrical.control.fuse-block.notes: Two-way fuse block 'adjacent to the control box on the wing valance' (Sec 33 para 1, photo 33.1): fuse 1-2 for the horns and lights that work with the ignition off, fuse 3-4 for the ignition-switched circuits; two spare 35 A fuses carried. MGOC Spares 606253A (Lucas 4FJ, 1962-69).

specs.label: Fuse rating
specs.note: Two spare 35 amp fuses are carried

electrical.control.flasher.name: Flasher unit
electrical.control.flasher.notes: 'A small cylindrical metal container in the engine compartment' (Sec 42 para 1), in a clip on the right inner wing (D).

electrical.control.relay.name: Overdrive relay
electrical.control.relay.notes: Overdrive relay unit (Fig 10.26 item 68), switched by the facia switch through the gearbox (isolation) and throttle switches, feeding the overdrive solenoid. MGOC 142169: 'rectangular metal can type', overdrive circuit on 3-synchro models. Placed on the left inner wing (D).

electrical.control.vacuum-switch.name: Overdrive throttle (vacuum) switch
electrical.control.vacuum-switch.notes: Item 74, 'overdrive throttle switch', in the relay's earth circuit. Fitted as a vacuum switch on the left of the bulkhead (MGOC, P5b note); its pipe to the inlet manifold is not modelled.

electrical.control.horn.name: Horn, Lucas 9H12
electrical.control.horn.notes: Two horns (Fig 10.26 item 23, 'Horns'), type 9H12, 3 to 3 1/2 A (p162). Adjusting screw and locknut under the cover (Sec 50 para 3). Disc form with a domed cover from the common Lucas pattern; mounted on the front panel behind the grille (D).

specs.label: Current
specs.note: Maximum current consumption 3 1/2 amps; Sec 50 para 2: 3 to 3 1/2 A

specs.ref: 1/4 in self-tapping or UNF screws into the panel

electrical.instruments.speedometer-case.name: Speedometer case
electrical.instruments.speedometer-case.notes: Smiths speedometer with odometer and trip, cable driven from the overdrive (Fig 10.26 item 45). Outboard of the tachometer for RHD (D: mirror of the LHD layout; question for Oliver). Held by the bracket, its two knurled nuts and the cable nut (Sec 46).

electrical.instruments.dual-gauge-case.notes: Dual gauge: mechanical oil pressure through the pipe from the engine (Ch 1 Sec 6 para 5) and the capillary temperature element (Ch 2 Sec 15) (Fig 10.26 items 42, 46).

electrical.instruments.toggle-switch.name: Toggle switch (lighting, wiper, heater, overdrive)
electrical.instruments.toggle-switch.notes: Early facia switches held by their lockrings (Sec 45 para 3); the overdrive switch (Fig 10.9 item 2) on the facia right of the binnacle. Which switches are toggles and which pull switches on the 1963 facia is from Fig 10.9 and is listed in the questions for Oliver.

electrical.instruments.pull-switch.name: Pull switch (panel lamp, map lamp)
electrical.instruments.pull-switch.notes: Items 1 and 4: the knob comes off by depressing the plunger in its shank, then the lockring (Sec 45 para 4).

electrical.instruments.ignition-switch.name: Ignition/starter switch, lock and key
electrical.instruments.ignition-switch.notes: Items 8-10: key switch with its starter position (the inertia starter's solenoid is energised from it); removed by the lockring behind the facia (Sec 45 para 2).

electrical.instruments.speedo-cable.name: Speedometer cable
electrical.instruments.speedo-cable.notes: From the angle drive on the overdrive rear casing (P5b, MGOC 120694) to the back of the speedometer (Ch 1 Sec 6 para 30; Sec 46 para 4: 'disconnect the drive cable'). Route through the tunnel and up behind the facia derived (D).

electrical.instruments.oil-pipe.name: Oil pressure gauge pipe
electrical.instruments.oil-pipe.notes: Disconnected at the engine on engine removal (Ch 1 Sec 6 para 5, photo 6.5). Route derived.

electrical.instruments.oil-union.name: Oil gauge pipe union
electrical.instruments.oil-union.notes: On the main oil gallery near the rear of the block (D: the gallery is the pressure take-off; Haynes photo 6.5 shows the pipe disconnected at the right of the engine).

electrical.instruments.capillary.name: Temperature gauge capillary
electrical.instruments.capillary.notes: Capillary from the thermal transmitter to the dual gauge (Ch 2 Sec 15 paras 1-3). Route derived.

electrical.instruments.transmitter.name: Thermal transmitter and gland nut
electrical.instruments.transmitter.notes: 'Unscrew the thermal transmitter from the cylinder head' (Ch 1 Sec 13 para 6); capillary type held by its gland nut (Ch 2 Sec 15 para 3). Its place on the head's right face ahead of No 1 plug is derived; P1's head has no boss for it yet (noted in PLAN).

electrical.lamps.headlamp-bowl.name: Headlamp body (bowl)
electrical.lamps.headlamp-bowl.notes: Pressed lamp body in the wing nacelle, with the three beam setting screws (Fig 10.7 item 4: vertical at the top, horizontal at the sides, Sec 34 para 6) and the grommet for the leads at the back. Depth derived from the nacelle; Fig 10.7 shows the four retaining systems used over the years, the early one being the combined adjusting and retaining screws (item 2), modelled here.

specs.ref: 7 in pre-focus/sealed beam bowl, Fig 10.7 proportion

electrical.lamps.light-unit.name: Headlamp light unit, 7 in
electrical.lamps.light-unit.notes: Sealed beam or bulb-type light unit (Sec 34 para 1); the lugs on a sealed beam allow one position only (para 10). Lens fluting simplified to vertical prisms.

specs.ref: Standard 7 in British headlamp unit (Lucas F700 class)

electrical.lamps.headlamp-rim.name: Headlamp chrome rim
electrical.lamps.headlamp-rim.notes: Hooked on the lugs at the top and snapped down, with the cut-out at the bottom (Sec 34 paras 1 and 5). Profile derived.

electrical.lamps.side-body.name: Side and flasher lamp body
electrical.lamps.side-body.notes: Wing-mounted type: the body held by two nuts behind the wing (Sec 35 para 2); photo 35.1. Rectangular on Oliver's car (photos 10, 20; P11b changed it from P10's lozenge): amber flasher inboard, clear side lamp outboard, chrome surround.

specs.ref: Oliver's photos 10, 15, 20: rectangular unit, scaled on the headlamp rim

electrical.lamps.side-rim.name: Side lamp lens rim
electrical.lamps.side-rim.notes: Lens and sealing rubber held by the screws (Sec 35 para 1).

specs.ref: Oliver's photos 10, 15, 20: rectangular unit, scaled on the headlamp rim

electrical.lamps.rear-body.name: Rear lamp body and plinth
electrical.lamps.rear-body.notes: Earlier version (Sec 36 paras 1-3): the stop/tail and flasher bulbs one above the other (photo 36.1), body held by three screws, the lens hooked over the upper lip and held by one screw at the bottom. Outline from photo 36.1.

electrical.lamps.rear-lens-red.name: Stop and tail lens (red)
electrical.lamps.rear-lens-red.notes: Double filament bulb: tail, and the brighter stop light (Sec 36 para 1).
