electrical.lamps.plate-lamp.name: Number plate lamp (plinth and cover)
electrical.lamps.plate-lamp.notes: Basic type: two lamps, one on each inside face of the rear overriders, cover, lens, washer and plinth held by two screws to nuts and distance pieces in the overrider (Sec 37 paras 1-2; photo 37.1).

electrical.loom.engine-bay.name: Main harness sleeving, engine bay
electrical.loom.engine-bay.notes: Braided sleeving over the main harness from the bulkhead grommet forward along the top of the right inner wing, across behind the grille and back along the left wing to the overdrive relay and throttle switch (early MGB harnesses are covered in lacquered cotton braid; the branches to the units leave it as bare wires). It fits the bundle it covers: its size on each run is the bundle's (mgb/wiring_layout.py). Hide it with the eye toggle to see the wires inside. Route derived.

electrical.loom.facia.name: Facia harness sleeving
electrical.loom.facia.notes: Braided sleeving over the harness from the grommet behind the facia, along behind the instruments and switches to the wiper motor, and down to the dip switch and the column switch. Route derived.

electrical.loom.rear.name: Rear harness sleeving
electrical.loom.rear.notes: Braided sleeving over the rear harness down the right-hand sill, up the heelboard, over the right-hand wheel arch into the boot and across the rear panel. Route derived.

electrical.loom.overdrive.name: Overdrive leads sleeving
electrical.loom.overdrive.notes: Sleeving over the overdrive leads from the relay down past the bulkhead into the tunnel to the gearbox switch and on to the solenoid (Ch 6 Sec 16). Route derived.

electrical.loom.bulkhead-grommet.name: Main harness bulkhead grommet
electrical.loom.bulkhead-grommet.notes: Rubber grommet in the bulkhead where the main harness passes from the engine bay to behind the facia (right-hand side, high). Position derived (mgb/body_layout.py HARNESS_GROMMET); its hole in the bulkhead is the body's (P11).

specs.label: Flange diameter
specs.ref: Sized round the harness bundle with a 6 mm lip

electrical.starting.drive-end-bracket.name: Starter drive end bracket
electrical.starting.drive-end-bracket.notes: Flange with two bolt ears that holds the motor to the engine (Sec 23 para 1: "held by two bolts"; Sec 25 para 3), a spigot into the starter aperture of the engine rear plate (P2) and the bush (item 20) for the shaft. The two bolts pass through the rear plate and screw into the bellhousing lobe round the starter pocket (P5a casing). Fig 10.4 draws the flange with its two holes and the boss; the ears' spacing is derived to fit inside the plate's starter lobe.

electrical.starting.yoke.name: Starter yoke and field coils
electrical.starting.yoke.notes: Four field coils on four pole shoes held by countersunk pole screws (Sec 23 para 1, "four field coil, four pole piece type"; Fig 10.5 item 30 pole shoe screw), brush windows at the commutator end under the cover band (item 31), and the field terminal post (25) through the yoke. The diameter follows the Lucas type number (M418, 4.18 in); the length is set by the room between the engine rear plate and the oil filter canister, which Haynes has removed first (Sec 25 para 2).

specs.label: Diameter
specs.ref: Lucas M-series type number (M418) read as the yoke diameter in inches

electrical.starting.cover-band.name: Starter cover band
electrical.starting.cover-band.notes: Band over the brush windows, loosened by its screw to reach the brushes (Sec 26 para 1).

specs.label: Width
specs.ref: Fig 10.4: about a quarter of the yoke length

electrical.starting.commutator-end-brack.name: Starter commutator end bracket
electrical.starting.commutator-end-brack.notes: Dished end bracket carrying the brush boxes and the commutator end bush (22), held by the two through-bolts (26).

electrical.starting.shaft-cap.name: Starter shaft cap
electrical.starting.shaft-cap.notes: Cap over the squared end of the armature shaft; a spanner on the square frees a jammed motor (Sec 24 para 2).

electrical.starting.armature.name: Starter armature and shaft
electrical.starting.armature.notes: Armature core, commutator (not undercut, Sec 26 para 8) and the shaft that runs back through the drive end bush to carry the drive, with its Woodruff key (18).

specs.label: Shaft diameter
specs.ref: Fig 10.4 proportion; the screwed sleeve slides on it

electrical.starting.pinion.name: Starter pinion and barrel
electrical.starting.pinion.notes: Nine-tooth pinion, shown at rest out of mesh ahead of the ring gear; the inertia of the pinion makes it run along the screwed sleeve into the ring when the motor starts. 9 teeth on the 120-tooth ring give the published 13.3 to 1.

electrical.starting.drive-sleeve.name: Starter drive (screwed sleeve, drive head sleeve, anchor plates, circlip)
electrical.starting.drive-sleeve.notes: Drive assembly 1 of Fig 10.4 less the pinion and main spring: screwed sleeve (9), drive head sleeve (5), rear and front anchor plates (8, 3) and circlip (2) at the shaft end (Sec 26 para 4).

specs.label: Outside diameter
specs.ref: Fig 10.4: about the anchor plate diameter

electrical.starting.terminal-post.name: Starter terminal post, nuts and washers
electrical.starting.terminal-post.notes: Items 24 and 25: the starter cable is held under the outer nut (Sec 25 para 1).

specs.label: Thread
specs.ref: 5/16 in stud, as the solenoid main terminals

electrical.starting.mounting-bolt.name: Starter mounting bolt
electrical.starting.mounting-bolt.notes: Two bolts (Sec 23 para 1, Sec 25 para 3), 30 lbf ft (p162): through the flange and the engine rear plate into the bellhousing lobe; the earth strap eye under the top one.

specs.label: Thread
specs.ref: 3/8 in UNF: the size that takes 30 lbf ft on this engine (rear plate large screws, P2)

electrical.starting.solenoid.name: Starter solenoid (remote)
electrical.starting.solenoid.notes: Item 4 of the early wiring diagram (Fig 10.26, dynamo cars): the inertia starter needs a separate solenoid switch (Sec 24 para 4: "a click should have been heard ... the solenoid main contacts"). Modelled as the Lucas ST950 pattern with two main studs and the small switch terminal on the cap and the manual push underneath. Its place on the right inner wing beside the control box is derived (body_layout.SOLENOID); see the questions for Oliver. MGOC lists the cables AHH5449 (battery to solenoid) and AHA6280 (solenoid to starter).

electrical.starting.starter-cable.name: Solenoid to starter cable
electrical.starting.starter-cable.notes: Heavy cable from the solenoid's starter stud to the starter terminal post (Sec 25 para 1). Route derived (D): up off the stud, inboard over the chassis leg and down onto the post.

engine.block.casting.name: Cylinder block
engine.block.casting.material: Cast iron, integral cylinders and waterways (Haynes p25)
engine.block.casting.notes: 18G block with three main bearings. Bore and stroke are published; the outer form is derived. The crank centre height comes from the published stroke, rod length and piston compression height. Water jacket and oilways are not modelled, so the model is solid where the real block is hollow. Firing order 1-3-4-2, No 1 cylinder next to the radiator (Haynes p20). External form (derived from Haynes Fig 1.8, Haynes photos 58.4, 61.1(a) and 55.4, and owners' photos of bare 18G blocks). Left side: a proud tappet chest panel with two openings and gasket faces, the camshaft tunnel showing as a shelf below it, the oil pump drive pillar under the skew gear, the blanked fuel pump flange (stud 12), the cast "1800" panel, the relief valve boss at the left rear (Haynes Sec 17) with plug 7 beside it, and the drain tap boss at the front. Right side: a straight water-jacket wall with the engine number plate pad below the deck (Haynes p7: plate on the right-hand side), two side core plugs, a ledge carrying the main oil gallery and the leaning distributor housing boss, then the crankcase wall with the oil filter pad and dipstick boss. Both sides: main web ribs and a pocketed sump flange.

specs.label: Deck to crank centre
specs.ref: Half stroke 44.45 (H p20) + rod centres 165.1 (H p21) + compression height 42.06 (FIA 3016)

specs.label: Length

engine.head.casting.name: Cylinder head

fuel.carbs.piston.name: Suction piston and needle
fuel.carbs.piston.notes: The tapered needle (item 19) is held in the piston by its screw (Fig 3.11 item 2); No 5 needle on the 18G (Haynes p66).

fuel.carbs.damper.name: Cap and damper
fuel.carbs.damper.notes: Top up the hollow piston rod with engine oil to 1/2 in above the rod (Haynes Sec 17 para 7, photo 17.7).

fuel.carbs.jet-front.name: Jet assembly (front)
fuel.carbs.jet-front.notes: Jet with its head and the feed tube from the float chamber (Fig 3.11 items 6 and 7).

fuel.carbs.float-chamber-front.name: Float chamber (front)
fuel.carbs.float-chamber-front.notes: Held to the body by a bolt through rubber grommets (items 22-26).

fuel.carbs.float-lid-front.name: Float chamber lid (front)
fuel.carbs.float-lid-front.notes: Fuel inlet union and overflow pipe (Haynes Sec 18 para 1); needle and seat inside (item 32).

fuel.carbs.heat-shield.name: Heat shield
fuel.carbs.heat-shield.notes: One shield between the manifold flanges and both instruments (Haynes Sec 18 para 5, photo 18.5).

fuel.carbs.distance-piece.name: Distance piece
fuel.carbs.distance-piece.notes: Composition insulating blocks between the heat shield and each carburettor (Haynes Sec 18 para 5).

fuel.carbs.flange-gasket.name: Carburettor flange gasket
fuel.carbs.flange-gasket.notes: Two gaskets either side of each distance piece, plus one at each manifold flange (Sec 18 para 5).

fuel.carbs.cleaner-case-front.name: Air cleaner case (front)

fuel.carbs.cleaner-bolt.notes: Two bolts secure each air cleaner to its carburettor flange (Haynes Sec 3 para 1).

fuel.exhaust.front-pipe.name: Front pipe (twin downpipes and Y-piece)
fuel.exhaust.front-pipe.notes: Two downpipes, one from each manifold outlet (the front one carries cylinders 1 and 4 through the Y in the casting, the rear one the siamesed 2/3 port: MGOC Spares "MGB exhaust systems"), each with a two-hole flange welded below a flared spigot that carries the sealing ring (photo 46.2). They drop beside the bellhousing, behind the engine rear plate, and run into a pressed breeches that necks down to the 1 7/8 in system pipe, which passes under the gearbox crossmember (Moss Motors 459-075: the head pipe "may touch the transmission cross member") to the centre silencer. Part of the one-piece welded system (Sec 46 para 1). Route and bends derived; downpipe size derived from the outlets.

fuel.exhaust.centre-silencer.name: Centre silencer
fuel.exhaust.centre-silencer.notes: Flattened oval case on chrome bumper cars (MGOC Spares "MGB exhaust systems"; twin perforated tube internals from July 1963), with rolled lock seams round the end plates, two pressed beads and a lock seam along it. Hangs under the left-hand floor beside the tunnel, 8 mm under the floor (mgb.underbody_layout FLOOR_Z), its underside at the published 4.2 in minimum ground clearance. Size derived (18 x 8 in section 80 mm deep).

fuel.exhaust.inter-pipe.name: Intermediate pipe
fuel.exhaust.inter-pipe.notes: From the centre silencer back between the tunnel and the left-hand battery carrier (P10), under the axle's left neck (Moss Motors 459-075: the system passes under the rear axle), under the left-hand handbrake rod behind the axle (P8) and out to the rear silencer. 1 7/8 in pipe (MGOC Spares GEX9008 U clamp 1 7/8 in).

fuel.exhaust.rear-silencer.name: Rear silencer
fuel.exhaust.rear-silencer.notes: Cylindrical (MGOC Spares: "the rear silencer was always a cylindrical type"), rolled end seams, dished end plates, a centre bead and a lock seam. Lies fore and aft behind the axle on the left, between the fuel tank and the left-hand road spring. Size derived.

fuel.exhaust.tail-pipe.name: Tail pipe
fuel.exhaust.tail-pipe.notes: From the rear silencer to the bumper line on the left (MGOC Spares: the tail pipe exits on the left-hand side; originally cut at 45 degrees). The rear mounting's pinch clamp grips it (Sec 46 para 3).

specs.label: Cut angle
specs.note: Tailpipe originally cut at a 45 degree angle

fuel.exhaust.sealing-ring.name: Exhaust flange sealing ring
fuel.exhaust.sealing-ring.notes: One on each downpipe's flared spigot, seating in the counterbore of each manifold outlet; "note the sealing rings" (Sec 46 para 2, photo 46.2). Two per car (Rimmer Bros fitting kit: "downpipe seals"). Size derived.

fuel.exhaust.manifold-stud.name: Downpipe stud

fuel.exhaust.manifold-stud.notes: Two per outlet, screwed up into the manifold's outlet flange either side of the outlet, across the car (D).

fuel.exhaust.flange-nut.name: Nut, downpipe flange
fuel.exhaust.flange-nut.notes: Brass so it does not seize on the hot stud (MGOC). Removed first; the pipe then drops away (Sec 46 para 2).

fuel.exhaust.gearbox-bracket.name: Exhaust bracket, gearbox (3-synchro)

Held under the two lowest rear side cover bolts on the left of the gearbox, where the pipe runs (D: the side cover face is the nearest machined face on the 3-synchro casing); its tongue joggles out to the strap. The two side cover bolts lose 4 mm of thread engagement to it.

fuel.exhaust.gearbox-strap.name: Exhaust strap, gearbox clip
fuel.exhaust.gearbox-strap.notes: A band round the system pipe whose two ears are pinched against the bracket's tongue by the front support bolt (Sec 46 para 3).

fuel.exhaust.strap-bolt.name: Front support bolt

fuel.exhaust.rear-bracket.name: Rear mounting bracket (body)
fuel.exhaust.rear-bracket.notes: Pressed angle screwed up under the boot floor behind the tank (P11b: two captive nuts), its tab hanging on the outboard face of the rubber mounting with turned-out edges. Form derived; "the two brackets under the car" (Ch 8 Sec 3 para 6) are this and the gearbox bracket.

partNumbers.by: MGOC Spares (screw, hex head, 1/4 UNF x 3/4)

fuel.exhaust.rear-mounting.name: Rear mounting rubber
fuel.exhaust.rear-mounting.notes: Bonded rubber block with a steel tube through each end: the bracket bolt through the top, the pinch clamp's ears and bolt through the bottom (cars to 1970: "a pinch clamp rear mounting arrangement", MGOC Spares). Size derived.

fuel.exhaust.rear-clamp.name: Pinch clamp half, rear mounting
fuel.exhaust.rear-clamp.notes: Two pressed halves round the tail pipe, their long ears either side of the rubber block's lower end. The "rear mounting pipe bolt" is loosened to slide the pipe out (Sec 46 para 3). Form derived.

fuel.exhaust.clamp-bolt.name: Rear mounting pipe bolt
fuel.exhaust.clamp-bolt.notes: Pinches the clamp halves' ears and the rubber block's lower tube; loosened to slide the tail pipe out (Sec 46 para 3). MGOC lists a 1/4 UNF x 2 3/4 bolt (BH604221) with the rear mount; with the block drawn here a 1 1/4 in bolt fills the stack, so the length is derived.

fuel.pipes.float-hose-front.name: Fuel hose, front float chamber
fuel.pipes.float-hose-front.notes: From the inlet union on the front float chamber lid down under the instruments to the tee ("disconnect the fuel pipe hose(s) from the float chamber(s)", Sec 18 para 1). Run kept below the jets and throttle return springs (D).

fuel.pipes.tee.name: Fuel tee
fuel.pipes.tee.notes: Joins the two float chamber hoses to the feed from the pump (D).

fuel.pipes.feed-hose.name: Fuel feed hose (engine end)
fuel.pipes.feed-hose.notes: From the tee toward the bulkhead; the rigid pipe to the pump at the rear of the car joins at the union and is added with the body.

fuel.pipes.breather-hose.name: Rocker cover breather pipe
fuel.pipes.breather-hose.notes: From the spigot at the front of the rocker cover to the spigot on the front air cleaner; disconnected first when the air cleaners come off (Ch 3 Sec 3 para 1) and renewed if perished. Routed over the front float chamber (D).

fuel.pump.body.name: Pump body
fuel.pump.body.notes: HP pump body (Fig 3.2 item 61): the pumping chamber flange, the outlet valve cage and outlet connection on top, the inlet connection on the side and the filter and plug underneath (Sec 6 para 1). Minimum delivery 7 Imp gal per hour (specifications). Inlet faces the rear for the pipe from the tank; Sec 5 para 6: inlet and outlet must be connected correctly.

specs.note: Minimum delivery, early models: 7 Imp gal (31.8 litres) per hour

fuel.pump.gasket.name: Pump body gasket
fuel.pump.gasket.notes: Either side of the sandwich plate (Sec 7 para 20, "with the gaskets interposed between them").

fuel.pump.coil-housing.name: Coil housing
fuel.pump.coil-housing.notes: Houses the solenoid and armature; the two cast lugs at the bottom (Sec 7 para 20) carry the pump on its bracket through rubber blocks; the earth connector (item 8) on its screw on the side boss.

fuel.pump.end-cover.name: End cover
fuel.pump.end-cover.notes: Over the contact breaker; the terminal nut, Lucar connector and insulating sleeve (items 29-32) on the end, the non-return vent valve (34) on top (Sec 8 para 6).

fuel.pump.sealing-band.name: Sealing band
fuel.pump.sealing-band.notes: Over the end cover joint, sealed with adhesive tape (Sec 7 para 28).

fuel.pump.filter-plug.name: Filter plug
fuel.pump.filter-plug.notes: Taken off with the filter (item 64) for cleaning (Sec 6 para 1, Sec 8 para 1).

fuel.pump.body-screw.name: Body screw
fuel.pump.body-screw.notes: Six screws, fitted finger tight and then tightened in diagonal sequence (Sec 7 paras 20-21).

fuel.pump.bracket.notes: Comes off with the pump on its two bolts and spring washers (Sec 5 para 5). An angle on the heelboard's rear face (mgb.underbody_layout HEELBOARD_X), the leg under the coil housing's lugs. Form derived.

fuel.pump.rubber-mounting.name: Pump rubber mounting
fuel.pump.rubber-mounting.notes: Between each lug and the bracket (MGOC Spares, part 2). Check it has not gone hard.

The suction side: an air leak here makes the pump run fast (Sec 9 para 1). Run derived.

fuel.supply.union-nut.name: Pipe union nut
fuel.supply.union-nut.notes: Tank stub, both ends of the tank hose's pipe joint, the pump inlet, and both ends of the pump hose ("undoing the nuts", Sec 5 para 4).

Held up under the boot floor by two straps (para 6). Plan size and depths derived for the early cars' 10 Imp gal, the tank sitting between the right-hand road spring and the rear silencer.

fuel.tank.rear-hanger.notes: A pressed channel on the clevis pin through the body tab (P11b), the strap bolt through its foot (Fig 3.9). Form derived.

gearbox.casing.casing.name: Gearbox casing and bellhousing
gearbox.casing.casing.notes: One casting: the bellhousing and the gearbox case (Fig 6.3 item 1). Bell: round bolting flange on the engine rear plate, two ears at the top for the upper bolts and a lobe round the starter aperture; a deep, nearly round shell over the flywheel ring gear and the clutch with six external ribs, its top sloping down to the box (Fig 6.3); a pocket for the starter pinion; the right-hand wall drawn in to a flat face round the oval opening the clutch withdrawal lever leaves through (dust cover over it, Ch 5 Sec 7); the slave cylinder pad on a web on the right (Ch 5 Sec 6). Box: the front wall carries the first motion shaft bearing and the front cover on eight studs; a large opening on the left for the side cover on a machined face (photos 4.20a, 4.21a); the sump under the laygear with the drain plug; layshaft and selector rod bores through both walls; a boss and locating screw for the reverse shaft (photos 7.6a, 7.6b); the rear wall carries the centre bearing housing (Sec 4 para 14), the selector rod detent block on two dowels (Sec 4 para 9) and the studs for the adaptor. Side of the side cover: left (D, see PLAN questions). The dipstick on an overdrive car is in the remote control housing (Fig 6.4 item 10), so the casing top only has the plug (item 5). Lubricant capacity with overdrive 5 1/4 pints, 3.36 litres (p111). Drain the overdrive as well (Sec 2 para 4).

gearbox.casing.front-cover.name: Gearbox front cover

It covers the layshaft end, which has a step that lines up with a cut-out in the cover so the layshaft cannot turn (Sec 7 para 7), and the selector rod ends. The sleeve forward carries the oil seal (item 8; renew it by drifting, Sec 5 para 32); the arm on the right carries the two lugs the clutch withdrawal lever pivots between on its bolt (Ch 5 Sec 7, photo 7.3; lug positions from gearbox_layout, P4). Check that it floats slightly on its studs so the seal centres on the shaft before tightening the nuts half a turn at a time in diagonal order (Sec 7 paras 7-8).
